newsitem.title: USA: Clintons' legal defense fund returns $640,000.
newsitem.headline: Clintons' legal defense fund returns $640,000.

text.p: A trust fund set up to help pay the legal expenses of President Bill Clinton and his wife Hillary on Monday rejected $640,000 in contributions, mostly raised by an Asian-American businessman, because the money may have come from improper sources.

The fund's executive director Michael Cardozo told a news conference that Charlie Trie, who said he was a friend of the Clintons from Little Rock, Arkansas, brought two manila envelopes containing $460,000 in small donations from individuals to his office in Washington last March.

"Mr. Trie represented that the donations were from U.S. citizens who were not federal employees, with a few exceptions there was no check or money order in excess of $1,000, and they appeared to be in full compliance," Cardozo said.
But further investigation strongly suggested the donations did not meet the fund's guidelines, he said.

"The manner in which they were received, the sequential numbering of certain money orders, the identical handwriting on the money orders, the religious aspect, all of these were factors in our decision to reject the contributions," Cardozo said.

The religious reference pertained to a second set of donations totalling $179,000 that appeared to have been raised through the U.S. congregations of a Taiwan-based religious group called Ching Hai, he said.
Although many of the contributions might have been legitimate, Cardozo said, the fund felt that under the circumstances the money should be rejected.
A White House official who declined to be identified said the Clintons felt the trust had made the right decision.
"We have great faith in the judgment made by the trustees as advised by outside counsel," said the official. "They made the right decision."
The official said that the trust had informed the White House of its review of the money, making contact only through the White House counsel's office.
